body:
GitHub issue #243.

## Problem

The in-session PreToolUse rails hook (plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/adlc-hook.mjs,
`rails()`) gates the STRUCTURED edit tools (Edit/Write/MultiEdit) only. Bash is
intentionally NOT matched — a shell cannot be reliably parsed in-session, and rail
mutations via Bash (`cat >> rail`, `perl -i`, redirects) are caught by the
UNBYPASSABLE rails-guard CI diff gate at commit time. This is a deliberate design
(documented in the code header and pinned by the test
`the PreToolUse rails matcher excludes Bash`).

The defect is HONESTY, not coverage: the frozen-rail denial message says only
'Edits to frozen rails are blocked during build.' An agent that gets blocked on an
Edit reads that as 'this rail is fully enforced', so when it later reaches for a
shell write (for ordinary reasons, e.g. appending test cases with `cat >>`) it
either believes it is still guarded (and is not) or believes it has escaped
enforcement (it has not — CI will reject the PR). Both mental models are wrong.
Observed live under #234 / T55: 89 lines landed on a frozen path via `cat >>` and
`perl -pi -e` with no in-session block, after an `Edit` to the SAME path was
blocked.

The issue explicitly does NOT ask to intercept all shell writes (impractical and
hostile to normal use; a heuristic would be evadable and give false confidence).
It endorses making the hook's SCOPE explicit in its own denial message as 'cheap
and honest, and may be the right answer on its own.'

## Required behavior

Amend the frozen-rail denial message (`rails()`'s final `denyRail(...)`) to state
its scope accurately: this in-session hook gates structured edits (Edit/Write/
MultiEdit); a shell write to this rail (redirect / in-place edit via Bash) is NOT
blocked here but IS caught by the rails-guard CI diff gate at commit time — so a
shell dodge does not escape enforcement, it only defers the failure to CI.

Do NOT route Bash to the rails matcher (the exclusion is deliberate and pinned by
an existing test), and do NOT add a shell-parsing heuristic that would pretend to
be a boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The frozen-rail denial reason names the hook's scope (structured edits only)
   AND that shell writes to a rail are caught by the CI diff gate, not silently
   permitted to escape. Verify by reading the message and a test asserting it.
2. A regression test asserts the denial reason for a real frozen-rail edit
   mentions the CI/commit-time backstop (so the message cannot silently revert to
   the misleading 'blocked during build' wording). Verify: the test is RED
   against the old message, GREEN after.
3. The PreToolUse rails matcher still EXCLUDES Bash (the existing design test
   stays green); no shell parsing is added.
4. All existing rails-hook tests stay green; the bypass/override wording and
   behavior are unchanged.
5. Full claude-code hooks test segment green and `npm run preflight` green.

## Constraints

- Message/documentation change only inside `rails()`; do NOT alter the
  allow/deny DECISION logic, the trust-root freeze, or the bypass audit path.
- Keep the message concise; it is shown to the agent on every rail denial.
title: rails hook: make the frozen-rail denial message state its scope (structured edits only; shell writes caught by CI)
